messages.subject: Using Ctags in rkward
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Am Thu, 29 Oct 2020 10:46:14 +0100
schrieb Vojtěch Zeisek <vojtech.zeisek at opensuse.org>:
> Dne středa 28. října 2020 22:10:29 CET, Thomas Friedrichsmeier
> napsal(a):
> > I can make it so that kate plugin actions will be active
> > whenever a script window is active.  
> 
> It would be definitely perfect to have such a nice feature. Can we
> look forward the next release? :-)

Ok, I have added that in master just now (as usual, it may be up to 24
hours for the automated builds to catch up). Please take a look.

Do note that we are relatively free, now, to assign menu actions from
kate plugins to one of the following contexts:
  - show them all the time
  - show them when a script window _or_ the plugin's tool window is
    active
  - show them only for the plugin's tool window

Which option makes most sense may differ from plugin to plugin, so
please provide feeback, if you think we can improve something.

Also, we can make some simple modifications, such as moving top-level
menus to a sub-menu. I've moved "CTags" to "View", for instance. But
again, I'll need the feedback of those who are experimenting with those
plugins.

Finally, Martin, perhaps you could write up a mini-tutorial on setting
up CTags inside RKWard?

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: Using Ctags in rkward
messages.body_plain:
> Ok, I have added that in master just now (as usual, it may be up to 24
> hours for the automated builds to catch up). Please take a look.

Thanks Thomas, this is perfect; I think it is a huge improvement for rkward!

> Finally, Martin, perhaps you could write up a mini-tutorial on setting
> up CTags inside RKWard?

Sure. A primer follows here, but I can also prepare an online tutorial 
including screenshots (if you want to include this tutorial on the 
website at some point, I can prepare one in Markdown):

---

- CTags has to be installed on the local machine, on Ubuntu this for 
example as follows:

* sudo apt install exuberant-ctags

- CTags by default does not have support for the R language, but can be 
added by the user. To enable R support, we can add the following lines 
to a file ".ctags" in the home directory (if it does not exist, create it):

--langdef=R
--langmap=r:.R.r
--regex-R=/^[ \t]*"?([.A-Za-z][.A-Za-z0-9_]*)"?[ \t]*(<-|=)[ 
\t]function/\1/f,Functions/

(I got this from Fong Chun Chan's Blog here: 
https://tinyheero.github.io/2017/05/13/r-vim-ctags.html)

- In rkward, activate the Ctags plugin:

* Settings -> configure rkward -> Kate Plugins -> check "CTags"

- Now, there should be a CTags button at the botton of the main rkward 
window (next to "R Console", "Help Search" etc.). Click the button and 
go to "Index targets". Here, you can click "+ Add" to add the directory 
that should be indexed by CTags. This has to be done for each directory 
where we work with R files (however, it works recursively, so if you 
index the upper most directory, all of the directories within are 
indexed as well)

- To use CTags, define custom key bindings:

* Settings -> Configure Keyboard Shortcuts -> Action CTags

I think in R, the important actions are "Go To Definition" to jump to a 
function definition (I use CTRL-Y) and "Jump back one step" (I use CTRL-Q)

---

It would be nice if anyone can test and verify that this works.

Cheers,

Martin

Am Sun, 01 Nov 2020 10:56:12 +0100
schrieb Vojtěch Zeisek <vojtech.zeisek at opensuse.org>:
> Perfect, thank You. :-) Will it appear in some upcoming version? I
> so, we using rolling-release distros would get in very quickly.

Well, of course it will be released, sooner or later. We do have daily
builds of the development version at least for Ubuntu:
https://rkward.kde.org/RKWard_Source_Repository.html

For other distributions, there are no automated builds, so far, but
in most cases building from source is not terribly hard, these days.
(I'm currently working on some larger stuff, but in a separate git
branch; the master branch is still very close to the 0.7.2 release.)

If this particular change WRT to kate plugins gets some decent testing
(hint, hint) and positive feedback, it may be possible to turn this into
a mini-release, soonish.

Regards
Thomas
